title: Grand River Transit service cuts and business plan
subtitle: Asset management plan, Schneider's Creek trail, Bleams Road opening and Weber Street turn restrictions also recommended.
overview: The committee dealt mainly with Grand River Transit (GRT). Ridership is down in early 2025, which staff linked to changes in student ridership. The committee recommended that staff carry out in-year service adjustments to save money {{vote:m5}}. These include removing two Cambridge school specials and some extra student-crowding trips. It also recommended approving the GRT Business Plan, with implementation subject to the annual budget process {{vote:m6}}.

The committee recommended approving the Region's Corporate Asset Management Plan {{vote:m7}}. The plan is required by regulation and affects eligibility for infrastructure grants. It reports a growing gap between renewal needs and available funding.

It also recommended a route for the Schneider's Creek multi-use trail in Kitchener {{vote:m4}}. On the consent agenda, it recommended opening Bleams Road as a regional road {{vote:m2}} and new turn restrictions at Weber Street East and Stirling Avenue North {{vote:m3}}. Council will consider these recommendations later. After the closed session, the minutes report no public announcement. The next committee meeting is August 12, 2025.

decisions.item: GRT ridership update and in-year savings
decisions.detail: The committee received the Q1 2025 ridership update and recommended that staff implement the in-year service adjustments to achieve operational savings.
The committee recommended approving the Grand River Transit Business Plan, with implementation subject to Regional Council's annual Plan and Budget process.
The committee recommended approving the Region's Corporate Asset Management Plan as set out in report EES-SAM-25-002.

The committee recommended approving the route alternative for the trail from Manitou Drive to Block Line Road and directing staff to proceed with detailed design and construction, pending property acquisition.

The committee recommended naming and numbering Bleams Road as Regional Road 56 between Manitou Drive and Wilson Avenue, with by-law amendments adding it to the regional road system, as a through highway with a 60 km/h speed limit.

decisions.item: Weber Street East and Stirling Avenue North
decisions.detail: The committee recommended by-law changes prohibiting left-turn and straight-through movements from Stirling Avenue at Weber Street in both directions, at all times.

debate: On school specials, one councillor was concerned about cutting Cambridge routes, citing limited transit options there and longer trips for students. Staff said the two routes carry few riders and that alternatives exist. Staff said affected students would face longer travel times, and that work is under way to help them before September.

Several councillors raised seniors' access to transit. Staff favoured travel training and better awareness of the affordable transit program over free fares. Councillors suggested free days once or twice a month as a pilot, and one said they would want free-fare options when the plan returns.

Councillors raised fairness and access questions on the business plan. One asked whether Cambridge fares should reflect the lack of LRT there, and staff were unsure of the case for zoned fares but agreed to look. Another noted taxi brokers' reluctance to collect fares on MobilityPLUS trips, and a councillor representing a township said township services have different needs.
A councillor asked for future reports to compare the cost of new roads with the cost of investing in transit. Staff agreed to add this to the tracking list.

On asset management, councillors asked how the plan fits into the 2026 budget and capital prioritization. They also asked about carbon and green infrastructure, and about changes to development charges. Staff said a funding strategy and a development charge report are coming, and one councillor said the figures show growth does not fully pay for itself.
